newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-INTERNAZIONALE MUST BE WARY OF UNFANCIED BOAVISTA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INTERNAZIONALE MUST BE WARY OF UNFANCIED BOAVISTA.

text.p: UEFA Cup specialists Internazionale, who needed a penalty shoot-out to see off the challenge of Casino Graz in the second round, were drawn against Portuguese side Boavista in Friday's third round draw.
Inter were taken to the limit by the unfancied Austrian side on Tuesday after having England midfielder Paul Ince sent off in extra time.

Boavista are not regarded as one of the heavyweights of the competition but Inter, bidding for a third UEFA Cup triumph in seven seasons, will not treat them lightly in view of their close shave against Casino Graz.
Spain's Valencia, conquerors of holders Bayern Munich in the first round, were paired with Turkey's Besiktas who beat Legia Warsaw in the second round.

Valencia will be without goalkeeper Andoni Zubizaretta for the home leg. He will be serving an automatic suspension for his sending-off in the second half of Tuesday's goalless draw with Slavia Prague.
The Spanish club qualified 1-0 on aggregate.
Valencia president Francisco Roig said his side were in buoyant mood having beaten the holders and Slavia Prague.
"The Turkish fans have a reputation for volatile berhaviour but we expect quite a lot of our fans to travel to Turkey where we will be playing for the first time.
"I don't think there will be any problems," he said.
The three German clubs to reach the last 16 managed to avoid each other in Friday's draw.
Hamburg face arguably the sternest test after being paired with Monaco, surprise conquerors of Germany's Borussia Moenchengladbach in the last round.
Karlsruhe meet Denmark's Brondby while Schalke take on Belgians Club Brugge.

The clash between English premier league big spenders Newcastle and French side Metz could be one of the best of the round, especially if world record signing Alan Shearer has recovered from his groin operation.

Both were impressive winners in their second round ties, Newcastle thumping Hungary's Ferencvaros 4-0 in the second leg on Tuesday for a 6-3 aggregate triumph and Metz ousting Sporting Lisbon 3-2 on aggregate.
Russell Cushing, Newcastle's general manager, said there was "a reasonable chance" that Shearer would be fit to play in at least one of the two legs.
The England striker was operated on last week and was expected to be sidelined for at least five weeks.
"I think our manager (Kevin Keegan) will be very pleased with the draw," said Cushing. "Naturally, we didn't want to play someone like Internazionale until later."
First leg matches are on November 19 and the second legs on December 3.
